column1: 1:1|In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:|Retains the precise date, both patronymics, and distinct offices.
1:2|The LORD of Armies says, “These people say, ‘The time has not come—the time to rebuild the LORD’s house.’”|Preserves the repeated time in the people’s quoted excuse.
1:3|Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet:|Retains the repeated prophetic messenger introduction.
1:4|“Is it time for you yourselves to live in paneled houses while this house lies in ruins?”|Keeps the emphatic you and the contrast between private houses and this house.
1:5|Now the LORD of Armies says, “Think carefully about your ways.|Gives the set-your-heart idiom a repeatable natural rendering.

1:6|You sow much but bring in little. You eat but never have enough. You drink but are not filled. You put on clothes but are not warm. Those who earn wages put them into a bag full of holes.”|Retains all five frustrated activities and the concrete leaking-bag image.
1:7|The LORD of Armies says, “Think carefully about your ways.|Repeats the exact wording of the recurring summons.
1:8|Go up into the hills, bring timber, and rebuild the house. Then I will take pleasure in it and be honored,” says the LORD.|Keeps all three commands and the read be-honored form.

1:9|“You expected much, but look—there was little. You brought it home, and I blew it away. Why?” declares the LORD of Armies. “Because my house lies in ruins while each of you runs to his own house.|Preserves the surprising divine action and the house/house contrast.
1:10|That is why the heavens above you have withheld dew and the earth has withheld its produce.|Keeps both withholding clauses and dew rather than generalizing to rain.

1:11|I called for drought on the land and the hills, on grain, new wine, and oil, on everything the ground produces, on humans and animals, and on all the work of your hands.”|Retains the full list of affected crops, creatures, and labor.

1:12|Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and all the remnant of the people listened to the voice of the LORD their God and to the words of Haggai the prophet, whom the LORD their God had sent. The people feared the LORD.|Keeps the two leaders and remnant together and all three divine-name occurrences.
1:13|Haggai, the LORD’s messenger, delivered the LORD’s message to the people: “I am with you,” declares the LORD.|Preserves the messenger/message wordplay and repeated sender identification.

1:14|The LORD stirred the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. They came and worked on the house of the LORD of Armies, their God,|Retains each spirit separately and lets the sentence continue into its date.
1:15|on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.|Keeps the closing work date complete and attached to the preceding action.
2:1|On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet:|Retains the exact second date and messenger formula.

2:2|“Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people. Say:|Preserves the three addressees and their formal titles.

2:3|‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not seem like nothing in your eyes?|Makes the three questions natural without softening the comparison.

2:4|But now, be strong, Zerubbabel,’ declares the LORD. ‘Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,’ declares the LORD. ‘Get to work, for I am with you,’ declares the LORD of Armies.|Preserves all three be-strong commands and all three declarations.

2:5|‘This is the word I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, and my spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.’|Keeps the compressed covenant-word construction, exodus reference, and abiding spirit.
2:6|For the LORD of Armies says, ‘Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.|Retains the time qualification and all four cosmic realms.

2:7|I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come. I will fill this house with glory,’ says the LORD of Armies.|Reads the desired things collectively with the plural verb, without imposing a personal messianic referent.
2:8|‘The silver is mine, and the gold is mine,’ declares the LORD of Armies.|Keeps both mine clauses and the material treasure connection.

2:9|‘The later glory of this house will be greater than the former,’ says the LORD of Armies. ‘And in this place I will give peace,’ declares the LORD of Armies.”|Retains this house, comparative glory, peace, and both declarations.
2:10|On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet:|Keeps the third dated message exact.
2:11|The LORD of Armies says, “Ask the priests for instruction:|Retains the priests’ role in giving instruction rather than reducing it to opinion.

2:12|‘If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and that fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, does the food become holy?’” The priests answered, “No.”|Keeps the indirect-contact distinction essential to the question and the full food list.

2:13|Haggai asked, “If someone made unclean by a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?” The priests answered, “It becomes unclean.”|Distinguishes direct corpse-related uncleanness from the previous indirect holiness transfer.

2:14|Then Haggai said, “That is how these people and this nation are before me,” declares the LORD. “So is all the work of their hands, and what they offer there is unclean.|Keeps the divine first-person assessment and the relation to offerings.

2:15|Now think carefully, from this day onward, about the time before stone was laid on stone in the LORD’s temple.|Preserves the temporal hinge while signaling the retrospective comparison that follows.

2:16|When someone came to a heap expecting twenty measures, there were ten. When someone came to the wine vat to draw fifty, there were twenty.|Preserves all four numbers while leaving the source’s unstated units nonspecific.

2:17|I struck you and all the work of your hands with blight, mildew, and hail, yet you did not turn to me,” declares the LORD.|Retains the three afflictions and supplies the return verb demanded by the elliptical relational clause.

2:18|“Think carefully, from this day onward—from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid. Think carefully!|Preserves the repeated summons and exact foundation date.

2:19|Is there still seed in the storehouse? The vine, fig tree, pomegranate, and olive tree have not yet borne fruit. From this day on, I will bless you.”|Retains the question, all four plants, and the promise before visible yield.
2:20|The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month:|Keeps the second message on the same date distinct.
2:21|“Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I am shaking the heavens and the earth.|Retains the named recipient and present participial action.

2:22|I will overturn the throne of kingdoms and destroy the strength of the nations’ kingdoms. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and riders will fall, each by his brother’s sword.|Keeps repeated overturning and the fratricidal ending.

2:23|On that day,” declares the LORD of Armies, “I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant,” declares the LORD, “and make you like a signet ring, because I have chosen you,” declares the LORD of Armies.|Retains all three divine declarations, the chosen servant, and the seal image without adding an institutional conclusion.
